capex_to_revenue.why: Capex has run steadily at 2.6% to 3.1% of revenue. Nine-month 2026 purchases of property and equipment were 91.3 against 93.9, so I hold about 2.9%.

quotes.quote: Digital transactions within the Cross-Border Payments segment increased 34% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the prior year period.

fade_years.why: A 10-year fade lets the margin and growth rates move gradually from the recovery path to the steady state, given the many moving segments.

long_run_op_margin.why: Margins have been 11.5% to 12.6% for the last four years. I take a long-run value near the 2025 level, since the digital mix and Payments Infrastructure support margin but the low-value digital transactions and remittance policy risk limit it. The 2019 peak of 17.3% was a different mix and is not a base case.

quotes.quote: Operating income of $171.6 million, a 12% decrease from $195.0 million

op_margin.why: Q3 operating income fell 12% on 1% revenue growth, and the guided Adjusted EBITDA of about $725 million implies a 2026 GAAP margin of roughly 11%. I assume a gradual recovery as Cross-Border Payments stabilizes, partly held back by higher purchase amortization and digital investment.

quotes.quote: Return on new investment at which growth adds no value (code, after the company's leverage): 0.0754.

return_on_new_investment_long_run.why: The current return on tangible capital (41.8%) is high because ATM cash is partly funded by third parties and the business is asset-light. New investment in acquired intangibles, ATMs and digital platforms should earn well above the 7.5% break-even but far below the current return, so I assume about 25%.

quotes.quote: We now expect approximately $4.375 billion of revenue
the last few months have shown stabilizing to modestly improving trends

rev_growth.why: Year 1 (2026) follows management's revised outlook of about $4.375 billion, which is roughly 3% growth on 4,244.2. Growth should then recover to 5-6% as digital accelerators (up 33% over nine months), Payments Infrastructure and CoreCard offset the retail remittance drag. Management calls the stabilizing trend in Cross-Border Payments 'fragile', so the recovery is not assured.

terminal_growth.why: A globally diversified payments company with about 77% of revenue outside the USD should grow near nominal GDP in the long run, so I set it close to the code anchor, slightly below.

risks.risk: US immigration policy and the remittance tax keep Cross-Border Payments depressed or deteriorating, with the 37% operating income decline persisting and digital growth too small to offset it.
Low-value digital transactions, ATM fee pressure and weak travel spend limit Payments Infrastructure revenue growth, leaving consolidated growth at 1-3%.
Structural margin erosion from higher D&A (CoreCard), cost inflation and agent commission pressure lowers the long-run margin.

debt_level_representative.why: Total debt of 2,020.8 at the base year-end includes funding for seasonal ATM cash, and indebtedness moved between 2,654.0 and 2,177.3 within a quarter in 2026, so the structural level is unclear.

situation.margin_position: The 2025 operating margin of 12.5% sits just below the 2024 level and well below the 2019 peak of 17.3%. In 2026 it is falling toward about 11% because Cross-Border Payments is weak (US immigration policy, remittance tax) while D&A and SG&A are rising, including CoreCard amortization. The margin is pressured by company-specific policy and cost factors, not a commodity-type cycle.

tax_rate_representative.why: The base-year rate is 30.2%, but nine-month 2026 tax expense of 121.4 on pretax income of 350.1 implies about 35%, and the filings do not explain the jump.

situation.why: 2025 was a normal growth year with revenue up 6.4% and margin 12.5%. The 2026 run-rate is already lower: nine-month operating income was 380.7 against 428.8, and management cut its full-year outlook to about $4.375 billion of revenue. The base year therefore probably overstates near-term margin, but the Payments Infrastructure and digital growth lines support a partial recovery.

fade_years.why: A 10-year fade lets the recent growth rate converge slowly to the terminal rate for a diversified three-segment business.

long_run_op_margin.why: The margin was 11.7%-12.6% in 2023-25 and the 2019 peak was 17.3%. I assume a return to about 12.5%. The range is wide because remittance policy, ATM fee pressure and low-margin digital mix are all unresolved.

quotes.quote: Operating income of $171.6 million, a 12% decrease from $195.0 million

op_margin.why: Q3 2026 operating income fell 12% on 1% revenue growth because of the Cross-Border Payments decline, higher SG&A and CoreCard amortization. I set 2026 near 11.3% and assume a gradual recovery to about 12.4% by year 5 as Cross-Border volumes stabilize.

quotes.quote: Return on new investment at which growth adds no value (code, after the company's leverage): 0.0754.

return_on_new_investment_long_run.why: The base-year return on tangible capital of 0.42 is very high because of the asset-light remittance and epay businesses. New investment includes ATM cash, terminals and acquisitions, so I assume a much lower 22%, comfortably above the 7.5% breakeven.

quotes.quote: We now expect approximately $4.375 billion of revenue, approximately $725 million of Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS growth of approximately 10%.

rev_growth.why: Management guides 2026 revenue to about $4.375B, about 3% growth on the $4,244.2M base. After that I assume remittance pressure stabilizes and digital accelerators, merchant acquiring, Ren and CoreCard lift growth to about 5-5.5%. Growth stays below the 8-10% of 2023-24 because transaction-heavy growth earns little revenue per transaction.

terminal_growth.why: A global payments network with about 77% non-USD revenue and emerging-market exposure supports growth near but slightly below the nominal anchor. Regulatory and immigration headwinds argue for caution.

risks.risk: U.S. remittance pressure (immigration policy, remittance tax) persists or worsens, and digital growth cannot offset retail declines
Margins stay compressed by cost inflation, low-margin digital mix and Cross-Border operating deleverage
Regulatory or card network changes to ATM fees, DCC rules or epay margins reduce returns on new investment

debt_level_representative.why: Debt of about $2.0-2.2B is partly seasonal ATM cash funding and partly structural, and the evidence does not separate the two.

situation.margin_position: The 2025 operating margin of 12.5% matches the 2023-24 level of about 12-12.6%. Margin is now falling because Cross-Border Payments (formerly Money Transfer) volumes are hit by U.S. immigration policy and the remittance tax. Costs, CoreCard amortization and digital investment are also rising faster than revenue. The nine-month 2026 margin is about 11.6%, and the full-year 2026 margin should be near 11.3%.

tax_rate_representative.why: The base-year rate is 30.2%, but nine-month 2026 tax was 121.4 on pretax income of 350.1 (about 35%), and the filings do not explain the jump.

situation.why: 2025 growth (6.4%) and margin (12.5%) are in line with the prior three years. 2026 is a dip from a policy-driven remittance shock, not a structural change. The firm's 2026 outlook (revenue about $4.375B, Adjusted EBITDA about $725M) implies about 3% growth and a margin near 11%. I assume partial recovery toward about 12.5% as digital accelerators grow and the U.S. remittance pressure stabilizes.

flags: Euronet completed the acquisition of 100% of CoreCard Corporation, an issuer processor. The company says the acquisition contributed to Payments Infrastructure revenue growth and added $4.7 million of non-cash purchase price amortization in the third quarter of 2026.
Euronet announced it signed a letter of intent with Diebold Nixdorf to collaborate globally on transforming ATM networks. No definitive agreement or terms appear in the evidence.

business_model.claim: Euronet sells electronic payment and transaction processing solutions over its own global network, platforms and technologies. Its customers are financial institutions, retailers, service providers and individual consumers.
quotes: Euronet is a leader in electronic payment and transaction processing solutions for Financial Institutions, Retailers, Service Providers, and Individual Consumers utilizing our global payments network, platforms, and technologies.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 segment descriptions.
business_model.claim: The company reports three segments. In 2025 the EFT segment was about 30% of consolidated revenues, epay about 28% and Money Transfer about 42%.
quotes: In 2025, the Money Transfer Segment accounted for approximately 42% of Euronet's consolidated revenues.

business_model.claim: In May 2026 the EFT Processing segment was renamed Payments Infrastructure and the Money Transfer segment was renamed Cross-Border Payments. The names changed but the segment composition did not. By revenue share, Payments Infrastructure was about 38% of revenues for the three months and 34% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. epay was about 25% and 27%, and Cross-Border Payments about 37% and 39%.
quotes: In May 2026, the Company changed the name of the EFT Processing Segment to Payments Infrastructure and the name of the Money Transfer Segment to Cross-Border Payments in order to more accurately reflect the products and services provided by these segments.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 EFT segment description.
business_model.claim: Payments Infrastructure (formerly EFT) earns recurring management fees, transaction-based fees, surcharges and dynamic currency conversion (DCC) margins from its ATM and POS network and from outsourced management contracts for banks.
quotes: The primary sources of revenues generated by our ATM network are recurring monthly management fees, transaction-based fees, surcharges, and margins earned on DCC transactions.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 and MD&A.
business_model.claim: Transactions on the Payments Infrastructure network grew 36.0% in 2025, but revenue per transaction fell from $0.10 to $0.08. The 10-K attributes this to high-volume, low-value digital transactions, so revenue does not rise in step with transaction counts.
quotes: As a result, our revenue growth will not correlate proportionately with the increase in our transaction volume growth.
The decrease in revenue per transaction is due to an increase in processing digital transactions with a high volume and a low value per transaction.

business_model.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 earnings release.

quotes: Constant currency revenue growth was driven by continued growth in merchant acquiring, Ren sales, and the fourth quarter 2025 acquisition of CoreCard, partially offset by continued economic pressures on discretionary travel spend which negatively affects international ATM cash withdrawals.

business_model.claim: The epay segment earns commissions or processing fees from mobile operators for prepaid airtime, and commissions from distributing other digital content, vouchers and physical gifts. Digital media content is about 77% of epay revenues.
quotes: primarily derived from commissions or processing fees received from mobile phone operators for the processing and distribution of prepaid mobile airtime and commissions earned from the distribution of other electronic content, vouchers, and physical gifts

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A epay discussion.
business_model.claim: epay is a lower-margin distribution business. Its direct operating costs are mainly commissions paid to retail merchants, POS terminal operating costs and the cost of vouchers sold. In 2025 these costs were $891.8 million and the gross margin was 24.9%.
quotes: Direct operating costs primarily consist of the commissions paid to retail merchants for the distribution and sale of prepaid mobile airtime and other prepaid products, expenses incurred to operate POS terminals and the cost of vouchers sold and physical gifts fulfilled.

business_model.claim: Cross-Border Payments (formerly Money Transfer, sold under Ria, Xe and Dandelion) earns transaction fees plus the margin between wholesale and retail foreign currency rates. Its main cost is commissions to sending and correspondent agents, booked in direct operating costs.

Sending and correspondent agents each earn fees for cash collection and distribution services, which are recognized as direct operating costs at the time of sale.

growth_thesis.claim: The digital accelerators introduced at the May Investor Day (Ria digital, merchant acquiring, Ren) are the main growth driver management points to: their revenue rose 33% over nine months and was 26% of year-to-date revenues. For this to continue, they must keep growing fast enough to offset the pressured retail businesses.
quotes: Revenue from the digital accelerators introduced at the Company’s Investor Day(*) increased 33% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and represented 26% of year-to-date revenues

growth_thesis.basis: Figures stated in the release; the condition is inferred from the segment results.
growth_thesis.claim: Digital transactions in Cross-Border Payments were 8.1 million, up 34% from 6.1 million. Continuing this requires the Dandelion platform and Ria/Xe digital channels to keep adding volume while the retail corridors stay weak.
quotes: Digital transactions within the Cross-Border Payments segment increased 34% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the prior year period.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the release; the conditions are inferred from the stated drivers and offsets.
growth_thesis.claim: Payments Infrastructure (formerly EFT Processing) grew revenue to $437.9 million, a 7% increase from $409.4 million, and active ATMs reached 58,420, up 4% from 56,431. Continuing this requires merchant acquiring, Ren sales and the CoreCard acquisition to keep contributing, and ATM cash withdrawals to hold up despite pressure on discretionary travel.
quotes: Constant currency revenue growth was driven by continued growth in merchant acquiring, Ren sales, and the fourth quarter 2025 acquisition of CoreCard, partially offset by continued economic pressures on discretionary travel spend which negatively affects international ATM cash withdrawals.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the release; the conditions are inferred from the stated reasons.
growth_thesis.claim: epay grew revenue to $294.7 million, a 3% increase from $286.5 million. Continuing this requires ongoing demand for higher-value digital content, merchant acquiring and promotional campaigns.
quotes: Constant currency revenue and operating income each increased 5% and adjusted EBITDA increased 6% as a result of continued demand for higher-value digital content, merchant acquiring and promotional campaigns.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the release and the 10-Q; the 'must be true' framing is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: The condition that matters most for total growth is whether U.S.-related remittance pressure eases. Cross-Border Payments revenue was $431.0 million, a 5% decrease from $452.4 million, because of immigration policy and the remittance tax. Management says recent months show stabilizing to modestly improving trends.
quotes: Pressure persisted primarily in the U.S. market, but the last few months have shown stabilizing to modestly improving trends.

More recently, the U.S. outbound remittance market has experienced lower transaction volumes due to changes in U.S. immigration policies and the implementation of the U.S. remittance tax, which have affected certain remittance corridors.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures and outlook stated in the release; the interpretation is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Consolidated growth is thin at present: third-quarter revenue was $1,161.1 million, a 1% increase, while operating income was $171.6 million, a 12% decrease. Management cut its full-year outlook to about $4.375 billion of revenue and about $725 million of Adjusted EBITDA. For growth to resume, revenue gains must outrun the cost increases.
quotes: We now expect approximately $4.375 billion of revenue, approximately $725 million of Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS growth of approximately 10%.

growth_thesis.basis: Debt and buyback figures stated in the release; the condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Growth funding depends on keeping the balance sheet in order: total indebtedness was $2,177.3 million, down from $2,654.0 million at June 30, and management says it will keep reducing debt to maintain its investment-grade rating. It also repurchased $50 million of stock in the quarter. Reinvestment and buybacks must therefore fit within that debt-reduction commitment.
quotes: The Company remains committed to reducing its debt balances in order to maintain its investment-grade credit rating.

material_events.basis: stated in the cited earnings release
material_events.claim: Euronet published a revised 2026 outlook, replacing the targets given at its May Investor Day. The new figures are about $4.375 billion of revenue, about $725 million of Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS growth of about 10%. The company ties the revision to immigration-related pressure in Cross-Border Payments, broader economic pressures and FX conversion rate changes.
quotes: We now expect approximately $4.375 billion of revenue, approximately $725 million of Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS growth of approximately 10%.

material_events.basis: stated in the cited 10-K and earnings release
material_events.claim: Euronet completed the acquisition of 100% of CoreCard Corporation, an issuer processor. The company says the acquisition contributed to Payments Infrastructure revenue growth and added $4.7 million of non-cash purchase price amortization in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: On October 30, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition of 100% of the outstanding equity of CoreCard Corporation.
Adjusted operating income includes a $4.7 million increase in non-cash purchase price amortization related to the CoreCard acquisition.

material_events.basis: stated in the cited earnings release; the signing date is not given
material_events.claim: Euronet announced it signed a letter of intent with Diebold Nixdorf to collaborate globally on transforming ATM networks. No definitive agreement or terms appear in the evidence.
quotes: Signed a letter of intent to collaborate globally with Diebold Nixdorf to transform ATM networks

risks.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 earnings release and the 10-Q MD&A; the mechanism is partly management's own wording and partly inferred.
risks.claim: Cross-Border Payments (formerly Money Transfer) is weakening: Q3 2026 revenue was $431.0 million, down 5% from $452.4 million, and operating income was $37.3 million, down 37% from $59.3 million.
quotes: which has persisted longer than we anticipated
Constant currency revenue was impacted by continued pressure from U.S. immigration policy and broader global economic uncertainty

risks.basis: Outlook figures and the exclusion wording are stated in the 8-K release; the risk of a further cut is inferred.
risks.claim: The company has already cut its 2026 outlook to about $4.375 billion of revenue, about $725 million of Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS growth of about 10%. The outlook excludes further moves in FX, interest rates and other factors, so it could be cut again.
quotes: This outlook does not include any further changes that may develop in foreign exchange rates, interest rates or other unforeseen factors.

risks.basis: Debt, availability and cash flow figures are stated; covenant stress is inferred from the 10-K risk language, and no breach is reported.
risks.claim: Leverage is meaningful: total indebtedness was $2,177.3 million at September 30, 2026, and nine-month operating cash flow fell to 252.1 from 381.9 (table in millions) while earnings softened. Credit-facility covenants require EBITDA and leverage ratios to be met.
quotes: We cannot assure you that we will have sufficient assets, liquidity or EBITDA to meet or avoid these obligations, which could have an adverse impact on our financial condition.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the 10-K risk factors.
risks.claim: Policy and regulation affecting remittances are a stated risk: the 10-Q ties lower U.S. outbound volumes to immigration policy and the U.S. remittance tax, and the 10-K warns that enforcement activity is keeping some customers away from agent locations.
quotes: More recently, the U.S. outbound remittance market has experienced lower transaction volumes due to changes in U.S. immigration policies and the implementation of the U.S. remittance tax, which have affected certain remittance corridors.

risks.basis: Figures are stated in the 10-Q income statement and the earnings release; the margin-compression mechanism is inferred.
risks.claim: Costs are growing faster than revenue. Q3 2026 revenue was 1,161.1 against 1,145.7, while total operating expenses were 989.5 against 950.7 (table in millions), and operating income fell 12%.
quotes: Adjusted EBITDA and operating income were impacted by continued cost inflation.

risks.basis: Share counts and EPS are stated; the dilution mechanism is inferred from the convertible-note proceeds and the adjusted EPS reconciliation.
risks.claim: Diluted share count is rising while basic shares fall: diluted weighted shares were 45,761,882 against 44,809,457, while basic shares fell to 37,289,653 from 40,331,347. Diluted EPS was $2.53 against $2.75, so dilution from convertible notes weighs on per-share results.

unresolved_questions.basis: The decline and management's commentary are stated in P6. Whether the stabilization lasts is not in the evidence.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will the Cross-Border Payments decline end? Q3 revenue fell 5% and operating income fell 37%. Management says the pressure has lasted longer than it expected, yet describes recent months as stabilizing to modestly improving.
quotes: Pressure persisted primarily in the U.S. market, but the last few months have shown stabilizing to modestly improving trends.

unresolved_questions.basis: The outlook and its exclusions are stated in P6. The Investor Day targets and the split of the cut are not in the packet.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will the revised 2026 outlook be achieved? The outlook was cut from the Investor Day targets, and the evidence does not show how much of the cut is immigration pressure, broader economic pressure or FX conversion rates.
quotes: We now expect approximately $4.375 billion of revenue, approximately $725 million of Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS growth of approximately 10%.

unresolved_questions.basis: Inferred from the F3 line items. The liquidity discussion that would explain them is cut from P4.
unresolved_questions.claim: Why did nine-month operating cash flow fall from the prior year? The statement shows large offsetting working-capital swings in receivables, payables and settlement items, and the evidence does not separate seasonal or settlement timing from underlying cash generation.
quotes: Net cash provided by operating activities | 252.1 | 381.9

unresolved_questions.basis: Inferred from the F2 comparison. The cause is not stated in the evidence.
unresolved_questions.claim: Why did nine-month income tax expense rise while pre-tax income was slightly lower? Tax expense was 121.4 against 95.8 and pre-tax income was 350.1 against 357.0 (table in millions), and the evidence does not explain the jump in the effective tax rate.

unresolved_questions.basis: The debt movement is stated in P6 and F1. The year-end level and refinancing plans are not in the evidence.
unresolved_questions.claim: How much of the debt level is structural and how much is seasonal ATM cash funding? The debt fell $476.7 million in Q3 on the seasonal return of ATM cash, and the balance sheet still shows 470.5 (table in millions) of short-term debt and current maturities.
quotes: Total indebtedness decreased by $476.7 million during the quarter, reflecting the seasonal return of ATM cash following the peak European travel season and cash generated from operations, partially offset by $50 million of share repurchases.

unresolved_questions.basis: The repurchase amounts are in F3 and P6. Future capital allocation and remaining authorization are not stated.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will buybacks continue at the slower pace? Nine-month repurchases were 200.0 against 441.9 (table in millions), $50 million was repurchased in Q3, and management says it is committed to reducing debt to keep its investment-grade rating.
quotes: The Company remains committed to reducing its debt balances in order to maintain its investment-grade credit rating.

unresolved_questions.basis: Transaction counts and the investment amount are stated in P6. Digital unit economics are not provided.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will digital growth offset the retail remittance decline? Digital transactions grew 34% while total Cross-Border Payments transactions fell, and the segment is spending about $6 million more on digital initiatives. The evidence does not give the digital revenue or margin contribution.
quotes: Declines in constant currency operating income and adjusted EBITDA were principally the result of the flow through of the revenue declines to the bottom line and approximately $6 million incremental investment in digital initiatives.

unresolved_questions.basis: The amortization and the letter of intent are stated in P6. CoreCard's standalone contribution and the terms of the Diebold arrangement are not given.
unresolved_questions.claim: How large are the benefits and costs from CoreCard, and what will come of the Diebold Nixdorf letter of intent? CoreCard added $4.7 million of incremental non-cash purchase price amortization in Q3, and the Diebold arrangement is only a letter of intent.
quotes: Signed a letter of intent to collaborate globally with Diebold Nixdorf to transform ATM networks

unresolved_questions.basis: The cost lines are in F2 and the commentary is in P6. The line-level breakdown is not in the evidence.
unresolved_questions.claim: What is behind the faster growth in operating costs? Q3 selling, general and administrative expense was 99.0 against 84.6 and depreciation and amortization was 39.5 against 34.8 (table in millions), so operating income fell while revenue rose. The evidence does not separate acquisition effects, FX, investment and inflation.
quotes: Adjusted EBITDA and operating income were impacted by continued cost inflation.
